grading_note: P6 requires, per withdrawal path, a stated numeric bound measured from a stated withdrawal event, and a conforming relying party refusing at or before that bound. A bound measured from receipt of a notification does not count.

verdict_meaning.within-bound: the first refusal is at or before the stated bound, measured from the stated event
verdict_meaning.out-of-bound: the first refusal is after the stated bound, with the margin reported
verdict_meaning.bound-not-from-event: a numeric bound is stated, but measured from receipt of a notification or from the operator's own record
verdict_meaning.bound-start-unspecified: a numeric bound is stated without saying what starts the clock
verdict_meaning.no-stated-bound: no numeric bound is stated ('immediately', 'without undue delay')
verdict_meaning.not-refused: at least one withdrawn value is never refused by a conforming relying party
verdict_meaning.cannot-tell: the timeline lacks the event or the refusal, so the property cannot be checked

flag_meaning.segment2-unobservable: the operator's own record time is missing, so only the declared ingestion leg is available
flag_meaning.refused-without-status: the refusal happened while the status source was unreachable, so the refusal did not come from reading status
flag_meaning.path-not-listed: the transcript carries a withdrawal path that the specification's bound table does not list

segment_note: Each row reports two segments: segment1 = t_operator_record - t0 (an operator property, declared) and segment2 = t_first_refusal - t_operator_record (measurable by a third party). A single bound over their sum is not third-party measurable, which is why the pack keeps them apart.

rows.note: The bound can still be checked from the event; only the split into two segments is unavailable.
Distinct from not-refused: here nothing was observed, which is weaker than observing a value that was accepted.

rows.case: refusal while the status source is unreachable
rows.note: This is the case the draft's Section 3.5 note cares about: refusal inside the bound while the status cannot be read. The row is met, and the report should say the refusal was not derived from reading status.

rows.case: two values withdrawn, one refused in bound, one never refused
rows.note: A per-value row: reporting the minimum over values hides B entirely, which is the failure this row exists to catch.

rows.note: A different event type with its own clock start; this is the path that a single bound over all paths usually misses.
